content: Each client is assigned to a single register page for detailed tracking and documentation. The following information is meticulously recorded: 1. Community-based ART Tool Facility Information: Facility Name District 2. Community Health Worker (CHW) Details: CHW Name CHW Contact Number CHW Village CHW District 3. Registration Dates: Date the register was initiated Date the register was completed 4. Client Identification and Contact Information: Unique ID First Name Last Name Phone Number Address 5. Client Movement and Mortality: Date the client moved out of the CHW catchment area (including the new location) Date of death, if applicable 6. Visit and Treatment Details: Visit Date Date the client started on an antiretroviral (ARV) regimen Number of pills remaining at the time of the visit Date of pill dispensing Number of pills dispensed Date of the next scheduled refill 7. Treatment Interruptions: Dates of treatment interruptions Reasons for treatment interruptions, which may include: 1. Severe illness or hospitalization 2. Drug stockouts 3. Financial constraints faced by the patient 4. Poor adherence to the treatment regimen 5. Other reasons (to be specified) 8. Assessment of Tuberculosis (TB) Symptoms: TB symptoms must be assessed at every visit. If any symptoms are present, the client should be referred for testing and treatment. Symptoms to monitor include: 1. Current cough 2. Fever 3. Weight loss 4. Night sweats 9. Other Health Problems: Additional health issues to be documented include: 1. Ankle swelling 2. Puffiness of the face 3. Breathlessness 4. Diarrhea lasting more than two weeks 10. Pregnancy and Family Planning: Indicate whether the client is pregnant (P) or on family planning (FP). 11. Referral Information: Referral date, if applicable, for cases involving TB, other health problems, or pregnancy. This structured documentation ensures comprehensive tracking of each client’s health status, treatment adherence, and any complications or interruptions in care.
